why: The PASS 85 frame-time receipt (docs/evidence/pass85/lane-r/frame-time-before.json, 2026-09-02T15:30Z) predates this lane's PASS 87 changes - 256 invisible terrain-proxy meshes, 256 ballistic surfaces, four crate-lid colliders, three art-prop colliders and a non-zero emissive across many vegetation and structure materials. 'Still 1.85x' was a present-tense claim about a scene that had since changed, so the skeptic refused it. This is the re-measurement at the shipped head, same instrument, same viewport, same paired method.
head: fe897216 (source unchanged since; dist built 2026-09-03T00:03 from it)
instrument: scripts/qa/measure-farcrysis-frame-time.mjs via scripts/qa/run-with-preview-server.mjs, installed Chrome headless, 1600x900, WebGPU, 20 s rAF sample after a 5 s settle, --disable-frame-rate-limit --disable-gpu-vsync
comfyui: queue empty (queue_running [] / queue_pending []) checked before the first and before run 3
pairing: each run measures atomic-acres and farcrysis back to back in ONE browser launch, so a ratio is always same-window

summary.verdict: NOT MET, and NOT WORSE than the PASS 85 figure either. Four paired runs at head give p50 ratios 1.34 / 1.83 / 1.44 / 1.89 (median 1.64, worst 1.89) against the PASS 85 single pair of 1.85. The spread is the shared workstation, not the arena: the atomic-acres control itself moved 12.7-16.3 ms p50 across the same four launches. The honest statement is a RANGE, not a point.

drawLoadComparison.note: This is the check the skeptic actually asked for: did this lane's added geometry enter the frame? It did not. The 256 terrain-proxy meshes are visible=false and castShadow=false, so they are in no render list and the scene walk skips them. MEASURED, PASS 85 -> at head: triangles 869,656 -> 866,727-866,937; meshes 253 -> 253-255; instances 93,268 -> 93,194-93,287; shadow casters 99 -> 99; distinct materials 222 -> 222-224; in-combat pipeline creations 0 -> 0 in all four runs. The emissive lift changed material VALUES, not the permutation count.
